meta.title: Alpine Ascents - Mountaineering Information
meta.description: Comprehensive mountaineering and climbing information portal.

styles.name: Hiking
styles.desc: Day walks on well-defined trails at low to moderate altitude. Basic fitness and equipment required.

styles.name: Trekking
styles.desc: Multi-day walking expeditions through mountains, often with porters and camping.

styles.name: Rock Climbing
styles.desc: Climbing steep rock faces using hands, feet, ropes and protection.

styles.name: Alpine Climbing
styles.desc: Lightweight, fast climbing in high mountains combining rock, snow and ice.

styles.name: Ice Climbing
styles.desc: Climbing frozen waterfalls and ice formations with ice axes and crampons.

styles.name: Expedition Climbing
styles.desc: Large-scale climbs to the world's highest peaks, often lasting weeks.

styles.name: Traditional Climbing
styles.desc: Placing removable protection while ascending, leaving the rock unaltered.

styles.name: Sport Climbing
styles.desc: Climbing bolted routes with pre-installed protection, focusing on difficulty.

styles.name: Bouldering
styles.desc: Short, powerful climbs on small rocks without ropes, using crash pads.

styles.name: Mixed Climbing
styles.desc: Combining rock and ice techniques with specialized tools and crampons.

techniques.name: Rope Management
techniques.desc: Coiling, handling and managing ropes safely during climbs.

techniques.name: Belaying
techniques.desc: Controlling the rope to arrest a climber's fall using a belay device.

techniques.name: Knots & Hitches
techniques.desc: Figure-eight, clove hitch, prusik and other essential climbing knots.

techniques.name: Rappelling / Abseiling
techniques.desc: Controlled descent down a rope using friction devices.

techniques.name: Navigation
techniques.desc: Map, compass and GPS navigation through mountain terrain.

techniques.name: Rock Climbing Techniques
techniques.desc: Footwork, handholds, jamming and crack climbing skills.

techniques.name: Ice Climbing Techniques
techniques.desc: Swinging ice tools, front-pointing and placement of protection.

techniques.name: Snow Climbing
techniques.desc: Snow slopes, self-arrest, step-kicking and avalanche awareness.

techniques.name: Anchor Building
techniques.desc: Creating secure anchors from natural and artificial protection.

techniques.name: Crevasse Rescue
techniques.desc: Rescuing climbers from glacial crevasses using pulley systems.

techniques.name: Glacier Travel
techniques.desc: Roped team travel across glaciers with crevasse awareness.

techniques.name: Alpine Start & Pacing
techniques.desc: Early starts, energy conservation and altitude pacing.

sheltering.name: Mountain Tents
sheltering.desc: Four-season tents engineered for high winds, snow and extreme cold.

sheltering.name: Mountain Huts
sheltering.desc: Staffed and unstaffed shelters along popular routes offering rest.

sheltering.name: Bivouac (Bivy)
sheltering.desc: Minimal overnight shelter on the mountain without a tent.

sheltering.name: Snow Cave
sheltering.desc: Shelter dug into deep snow for insulation and wind protection.

sheltering.name: Igloo & Snow Trench
sheltering.desc: Structures built from compacted snow blocks or trenches.

sheltering.name: Emergency Shelters
sheltering.desc: Lightweight bivy sacks and bothy bags for emergencies.

sheltering.name: Base Camp
sheltering.desc: Main expedition camp at the foot of the mountain.

sheltering.name: High / Advance Camps
sheltering.desc: Intermediate camps at higher altitudes for acclimatization.

hazards.name: Avalanche
hazards.prevention: Check avalanche forecasts, avoid steep slopes after heavy snow, carry beacons and probes.
hazards.desc: Rapid snow slides that can bury climbers under tonnes of snow.

hazards.name: Rockfall
hazards.prevention: Wear helmets, climb early before thaw, avoid loose rock bands.
hazards.desc: Falling rocks dislodged by weather, climbers or wildlife.

hazards.name: Altitude Sickness
hazards.prevention: Ascend gradually, acclimatize, stay hydrated, descend if symptoms worsen.
hazards.desc: AMS, HAPE and HACE caused by low oxygen at altitude.

hazards.name: Hypothermia
hazards.prevention: Layer clothing, stay dry, eat regularly, watch for shivering.
hazards.desc: Dangerous drop in core body temperature.

hazards.name: Frostbite
hazards.prevention: Protect extremities, keep warm, monitor exposed skin.
hazards.desc: Freezing of skin and tissues in extreme cold.

hazards.name: Extreme Weather
hazards.prevention: Check forecasts, carry storm gear, descend before storms hit.
hazards.desc: Sudden storms with high winds and whiteout conditions.

hazards.name: Lightning
hazards.prevention: Avoid ridges and summits during storms, seek lower ground.
hazards.desc: Electrical strikes especially dangerous on exposed ridges.

hazards.name: Crevasses
hazards.prevention: Rope up on glaciers, probe snow bridges, learn rescue.
hazards.desc: Hidden cracks in glaciers that can swallow climbers.

hazards.name: Falls
hazards.prevention: Use ropes and protection, check anchors, climb within ability.
hazards.desc: The most common cause of mountaineering accidents.

hazards.name: Exhaustion
hazards.prevention: Pace yourself, rest regularly, eat high-energy food.
hazards.desc: Physical and mental fatigue reducing coordination and judgment.

hazards.name: Dehydration
hazards.prevention: Drink 3-4 litres daily, monitor urine color, carry purification.
hazards.desc: Fluid loss increased by altitude and respiration in dry air.

equipment.name: Climbing Helmet
equipment.desc: Protects head from rockfall and impacts.

equipment.name: Climbing Harness
equipment.desc: Waist and leg straps connecting climber to rope.

equipment.name: Rope
equipment.desc: Dynamic rope to absorb fall energy.

equipment.name: Carabiners
equipment.desc: Metal loops connecting rope to protection.

equipment.name: Ice Axe
equipment.desc: Multi-purpose tool for ice, snow and self-arrest.

equipment.name: Crampons
equipment.desc: Metal spikes strapped to boots for ice traction.

equipment.name: Mountaineering Boots
equipment.desc: Insulated, stiff-soled boots for snow and ice.

equipment.name: Backpack
equipment.desc: Carries gear, food and water on the climb.

equipment.name: Sleeping Bag
equipment.desc: Insulated bag rated for extreme cold.

organizations_intro: A network of mountaineering federations, clubs and agencies that support climbers worldwide with guidance, permits and training.
